title: Number lines: most-missed skills (easier to harder)

questions.q: A number line goes from 0 to 1 with marks at every 0.1. Which point is farther to the right: 0.4 or 0.9?
questions.why: 9 tenths is farther from 0 than 4 tenths, so 0.9 is farther right and greater.

questions.q: Which fraction is closest to 0 on a number line?
questions.why: The bigger the bottom number, the smaller each piece. 1/10 has the smallest pieces, so it is closest to 0.

questions.q: Each whole on a number line is cut into 4 equal parts. A point is on the 5th mark after 0. Which mixed number is it?
questions.why: 4 fourths make 1 whole, so the 5th mark is 1 whole and 1 more fourth: 1 1/4.

questions.q: Which is greater: 0.7 or 0.65? Think about where each sits on a number line.
questions.why: 0.7 = 0.70 = 70 hundredths. 65 hundredths is less, so 0.7 is farther right. More digits does not mean bigger.

questions.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest (left to right on a number line)?
questions.why: Write them with hundredths: 0.35, 0.40, 0.50. Those go up in order.

questions.q: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 10 equal parts. A point is halfway between the 6th and 7th marks. Which hundredths decimal is it? (Hint: halfway between 0.6 and 0.7.)
A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 100 equal parts. A point is on the 37th mark. Which decimal and fraction is it?
questions.why: 100 equal parts means hundredths. 37 hundredths = 37/100 = 0.37. It must be less than 1, so not 3.7.

questions.q: Which decimal is between 0.2 and 0.3 on a number line?
questions.why: Write 0.2 and 0.3 as 0.20 and 0.30. 0.25 sits halfway between them.

questions.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
questions.why: Use thousandths: 0.570, 0.580, 0.600, 0.605. Those go up in order.
